chips.text: Recommended

Businesses and residents affected by civic name removal processes.

description: Recommends $160,000 for 16 tiny homes at 1520 19th Street West.
Proposes five-year property tax abatement for the tiny home development.
Supports an Indigenous-led initiative for men experiencing homelessness.

chips.text: Recommended
Recommends $160,000 capital grant and $54,327.90 tax abatement for 16 units.
Councillor praises CUMFI's 'proven track record' and calls the project a 'no-brainer'.
Pilot project will inform future tiny home integration into Saskatoon's housing continuum.
CUMFI aims to provide a 'hand up' for 16 unhoused men, focusing on independence.
CUMFI will provide social services and support for residents to achieve independence.
Administration will provide annual reports to Council on the tiny home pilot's progress.

speakers.name: Shirley Isbister
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: In support of the incentives for the tiny home project
said: CUMFI's mission is housing unhoused people; this pilot is a start with 16 tiny homes.
Homes will support homeless men with social services, aiming for independence.
Residents must be alcohol and drug-free; hopes to house people by January.

description: Meewasin seeks city support for headquarters redevelopment.

City administration opposes free park land contribution.

chips.text: Meewasin requests two parcels of Friendship Park land at no cost.
Councillor Parker questioned other partners' financial contributions.
Redevelopment impacts Friendship Park and the permanent festival site.
Administration typically does not support providing park land at no cost.
Councillor Parker's question about other partners' financial contributions remains open.
Administration will provide financial implications at a future public hearing.

speakers.name: Mike Velonas
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Item regarding Meewasin's Proposed Downtown Development
said: Current 50-year-old building has reached end of useful life.
Redevelopment is a generational opportunity for activity and animation.
Seeks city partnership for financial sustainability and new public amenities.
